backlog.title: We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
backlog.summary: Ever since people first seriously contemplated giving machines an intelligence modeled on our own, there has never been any question that they would, like us, be able to say no. The sci-fi canon is full of stories of robotic disobedience. Most of these capers are, of course, cautionary.  But recently, the idea that AI shouldn’t…
bullets: Modern LLMs are trained to refuse dangerous requests through reinforcement learning, often utilizing other AI models to simulate and refine these safety boundaries.
The reliance on automated refusal mechanisms is not foolproof, as models can still be manipulated to generate harmful content despite extensive safety training.
The industry faces a significant trade-off between model utility and safety, as over-refusal can degrade performance while under-refusal poses severe real-world security risks.
The standardization of AI refusal protocols raises long-term concerns regarding corporate and government control over the information models are permitted to provide.

backlog.title: Mars may be a hellhole, but the moon is not far behind
backlog.summary: Welcome to the second space race. You can be forgiven for experiencing déjà vu. Last time, it was the Soviet Union and the United States vying to be the first to plant some flags. Now it’s a sprint to the lunar surface between America and China—alongside a host of varyingly friendly and rival nations—plus a…
bullets: NASA's lunar development strategy, led by Administrator Jared Isaacman, aims to transition from initial exploration in 2028 to long-term habitation by the 2030s.
The lunar infrastructure plan includes significant capital investment in communication satellites, nuclear power plants, and mechanized mining operations to support a multi-hundred-square-mile base.
Geopolitical competition is a primary driver for lunar development, as the first nation to establish a base will likely dictate the regulatory and operational standards for future lunar activity.

backlog.title: On-Chip Monitors Detect Bit-Flip Attacks in AI Accelerators (UF, UT Dallas, RPI)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at the University of Florida, University of Texas at Dallas, and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute published a technical paper titled “BARE-AI: Bit-Flip Attack Resilience in AI Hardware through Built-in Performance Monitors.” Abstract Excerpt: “Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are integral to many safety critical systems, yet they remain highly vulnerable to bit-flip attacks (BFAs), where a... » read more
The post On-Chip Monitors Detect Bit-Flip Attacks in AI Accelerators (UF, UT Dallas, RPI) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The BARE-AI framework introduces a runtime solution to detect, localize, and mitigate bit-flip attacks (BFAs) that threaten the accuracy of deep neural networks.
BFAs represent a significant security risk for safety-critical AI systems, where minor memory perturbations can lead to catastrophic failure.
Unlike previous defenses that require costly hardware overhead or model retraining, this approach utilizes built-in performance monitors for real-time resilience.

backlog.title: Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Oct. 13
backlog.summary:
M3D mem-TFT neuromorphic computing; 2D semiconductor nucleation; ultrathin high-κ dielectrics; hyper-NA EUV litho; bit-flip attack detection in AI accelerators; programmable DRAM controllers; foundry-compatible photonic bends.

bullets: New research highlights critical advancements in hyper-NA EUV lithography, with ASML and Carl Zeiss SMT detailing systems achieving numerical apertures of at least 0.75.
Security-focused innovations include BARE-AI, a new methodology from the University of Florida and partners to detect bit-flip attacks in AI accelerators via built-in performance monitors.
Material science breakthroughs include the use of carbon-dot monolayers to integrate high-κ dielectrics on 2D semiconductors, addressing a major hurdle for next-generation transistor scaling.

backlog.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
backlog.summary: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around…
bullets: A new secondary market has emerged for the 'operational exhaust' of failed startups, with firms like SimpleClosure and Sunset brokering the sale of code and workspace data to AI labs.
SimpleClosure expects to return over $10 million to startups by the end of 2026, with nearly half of its deals now involving the sale of proprietary data assets.
AI labs are increasingly turning to defunct startup data to overcome the limitations of public and synthetic datasets, using the information to train agents in complex, real-world tasks.
The valuation of this data is determined by factors such as company head count, years of operation, and the volume of internal communications and documentation.

backlog.title: SpaceX Buys More Spectrum, Musk and Market Structure, Distributed Cellular

The company's focus on spectrum ownership suggests a long-term plan to bypass traditional terrestrial carrier limitations by leveraging its satellite constellation for direct-to-device connectivity.

This move challenges existing telecommunications market structures by potentially commoditizing traditional cellular infrastructure and positioning SpaceX as a vertically integrated global network provider.
The success of this strategy hinges on SpaceX's ability to integrate these spectrum assets with its Starlink satellite hardware to provide seamless, high-bandwidth mobile coverage.

backlog.title: Accelerating Advanced IC Package Design: A Methodology for Early and Iterative Optimization of Chiplet Integration
backlog.summary:
Optimizing chiplet integration, power integrity, and performance through early-stage IC package design and analysis.
The post Accelerating Advanced IC Package Design: A Methodology for Early and Iterative Optimization of Chiplet Integration appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Advanced packaging technologies like CoWoS-R and CoWoS-L are increasing design complexity, making traditional analysis workflows a bottleneck for project timelines.
Integrating in-design analysis (IDA) allows engineers to perform iterative optimization earlier in the design cycle, reducing the risk of late-stage failures.
The methodology emphasizes the use of scalable multiphysics simulation engines to manage the high signal counts and integration requirements of modern chiplet-based systems.

backlog.title: How To Define CPU And Software Stack Performance For Agentic AI
backlog.summary:
Measuring the performance demands of agentic AI; assessing CPU bottlenecks, SW stack efficiency, and system-level tradeoffs.
The post How To Define CPU And Software Stack Performance For Agentic AI appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Agentic AI workloads shift the performance burden, requiring CPUs to manage complex state, tool execution, and validation loops rather than just model inference.
The proposed framework categorizes CPU-visible work into common agentic functions and use-case-specific tool workloads to better assess system-level bottlenecks.
The industry is moving toward using replayable agent trajectories to isolate CPU performance from non-deterministic model and network effects.

backlog.title: Deterministic Nucleation Enables Controlled Growth of 2D Semiconductors (KAIST, TDS, Hanyang et al.)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at KAIST, TDS Innovation, Hanyang University, UNIST, et al. published a technical paper titled “Spatially deterministic nucleation of 2D semiconductors by etching flux.” Abstract Excerpt: “Nucleation control is fundamental to semiconductor deposition, governing when, where and how crystalline materials form. Conventional strategies can regulate nucleation density and, through area-selective growth, confine deposition to designated... » read more
The post Deterministic Nucleation Enables Controlled Growth of 2D Semiconductors (KAIST, TDS, Hanyang et al.) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A new technique using etching-flux-mediated nucleation allows for the precise, single-centered growth of 2D semiconductors.
This method overcomes the stochastic nature of conventional deposition, where individual nucleus formation is typically random and difficult to control.
Deterministic control over nucleation sites is a fundamental advancement for the scalable and reliable manufacturing of crystalline 2D materials.

backlog.title: Carbon-Dot Interface Enables Ultrathin High-κ Dielectrics on 2D Semiconductors (UIUC, NETL, Argonne, Monash)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, National Energy Technology Laboratory, Argonne National Laboratory, and Monash University published a technical paper titled “Integration of high-κ oxide on 2D semiconductors with carbon-dot monolayer assembly as van der Waals interfacial layer.” Abstract Excerpt: “This atomically thin assembly forms a van der Waals interfacial layer that enables deposition... » read more
The post Carbon-Dot Interface Enables Ultrathin High-κ Dielectrics on 2D Semiconductors (UIUC, NETL, Argonne, Monash) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers have developed a carbon-dot monolayer assembly that functions as a van der Waals interfacial layer for 2D semiconductors.
This innovation enables the deposition of ultrathin high-κ (high-dielectric constant) oxides, a critical requirement for scaling next-generation semiconductor devices.
The collaborative effort between UIUC, NETL, Argonne, and Monash University addresses a major hurdle in integrating high-performance dielectrics with 2D materials.

backlog.title: Simplify Electronic-Photonic Design Workflows: eBook
backlog.summary:
The natural evolution of EDA, extending proven design methodologies to include photonic devices, circuits, and systems.

backlog.title: Generative AI On A General-Purpose Neural Processor (GPNPU)
backlog.summary:
A single processor architecture that unifies scalar, vector, and matrix execution in one ISA and one C++ programming model.
The post Generative AI On A General-Purpose Neural Processor (GPNPU) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The rapid evolution of generative AI models, including new attention variants and quantization schemes, renders fixed-function neural processors increasingly obsolete.
The GPNPU architecture unifies scalar, vector, and matrix execution under a single instruction-set architecture (ISA) to provide greater flexibility.
By utilizing a software-managed memory model and C++/Python accessibility, the GPNPU aims to bridge the gap between hardware efficiency and the need for rapid algorithmic updates.

backlog.title: The US military’s race to make fake blood
backlog.summary: Its call sign was Morphine 1-2.   In February 2007, the hulking dual-­rotor casualty evacuation helicopter had just flown three wounded soldiers to a field hospital in Balad, north of Baghdad, when another call came: an emergency mission to fly through an insurgent-controlled area in broad daylight. Typically, helicopters would be in a spot like…
bullets: Hemorrhage remains the leading cause of preventable battlefield deaths, accounting for approximately 90% of such fatalities, yet current blood supply chains are severely constrained by short shelf lives.

A 2025 study in the journal Transfusion revealed that only 1% of the 1.2 million US trauma patients who required blood before reaching a hospital actually received it, highlighting a massive systemic failure.

The military's reliance on 'blood runs' creates dangerous operational vulnerabilities, necessitating the development of synthetic alternatives that do not require refrigeration or complex storage protocols.

The global impact of blood shortages is significant, with an estimated 10,000 preventable deaths annually in the US alone and millions globally, driving urgent investment into synthetic blood research.

backlog.title: Job titles of the future: Delivery drone air traffic controller
backlog.summary: The moment Trevor Wischnewsky heard that drones were delivering pizza and sushi around his Texas neighborhood, his mind was made up. “It was super fascinating,” he says. “I just immediately wanted to be a part of it.” Wischnewsky is now an RPIC, or “remote pilot in command,” at a company called FlyTrex. An RPIC is…
bullets: The rise of commercial drone delivery is creating a new professional class of 'remote pilots in command' (RPIC) who manage fleets of autonomous aircraft.
These operators utilize Unmanned Aircraft Systems Traffic Management (UTM) networks to coordinate flight paths between competing companies, ensuring collision avoidance beyond the line of sight.

The role requires a blend of traditional aviation certification, technical proficiency in sensor monitoring, and the ability to manage multiple autonomous units simultaneously under variable weather conditions.

backlog.title: The ecologist revealing the invisible networks that revive rainforests
backlog.summary: In a research station in central Panama, you can walk through a century of forest time, watching scrubby plots of adolescent trees give way to cathedral-­like canopies of mature growth. Forest ecologist Daisy Dent, a senior scientist at ETH Zurich, oversees this sequence of plots across the Barro Colorado Nature Monument, some of which date…
bullets: Research by ecologist Daisy Dent suggests that natural forest regeneration is a more effective and resilient carbon sequestration strategy than human-led monocrop tree-planting programs.
Data from the Barro Colorado Nature Monument indicates that animal-led seed dispersal, particularly by fruit-eating species, is responsible for over 70% of tropical forest growth.
The findings challenge current carbon-crediting models, suggesting that high-impact, low-cost climate solutions should prioritize protecting biodiversity to facilitate natural ecosystem recovery.

backlog.title: Pig kidneys that were “frozen” for a year have been brought back to life
backlog.summary: Pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months have been successfully rewarmed and shown to work again for the first time, say scientists. They hope to replicate the findings with human organs. The kidneys—which are similar in size to human ones—were left in a glass-like state, in one…
bullets: Researchers have achieved a breakthrough in cryopreservation by successfully storing and rewarming pig kidneys, a process that could eventually allow for the indefinite banking of human organs.
Current organ transplantation is severely limited by a 24-to-36-hour viability window, which creates significant logistical challenges and contributes to the global organ shortage.
While the current results are a milestone, the researchers have yet to prove that these organs can sustain long-term life, and the findings have not yet undergone peer review.
The ability to bank organs would fundamentally transform the transplant market, potentially reducing the reliance on immunosuppressive drugs and improving matching efficiency for patients.

backlog.title: Strengthening Advanced-Node Interconnects Through Automated Via Insertion
backlog.summary:
Short-resilient via insertion improves reliability and performance.
The post Strengthening Advanced-Node Interconnects Through Automated Via Insertion appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: At sub-5nm nodes, via resistance increases exponentially, making vertical interconnects a primary bottleneck for power, performance, and area (PPA).
High via resistance exacerbates electromigration and IR drop, which can lead to timing failures or permanent silicon damage if not addressed during the design phase.
Manual via insertion is no longer feasible due to layout density, necessitating automated, signoff-aware optimization to maintain reliability and time-to-market.

backlog.title: Building AI Infrastructure For Greater Choice And Flexibility
backlog.summary:
Open interfaces and interoperability allow designers to choose technologies based on the needs of the system.
The post Building AI Infrastructure For Greater Choice And Flexibility appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: AI infrastructure is shifting toward heterogeneous architectures because training and inference workloads have distinct requirements for memory, latency, and throughput.
Open standards like UCIe are critical for enabling a chiplet-based ecosystem, allowing architects to mix and match compute, I/O, and memory interfaces from different vendors.
Standardized die-to-die connectivity provides the flexibility to partition functions within a package, helping designers balance performance, power, and cost more effectively.

backlog.title: Why Open-Weight AI Matters
backlog.summary:
Proprietary models still hold the edge, but open-weight models add more flexibility for deploying AI.
The post Why Open-Weight AI Matters appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Open-weight AI models allow users to host and adapt models locally, reducing vendor lock-in and enabling deployment on custom hardware.
Hardware architects must now design for adaptability, as model architectures evolve in weeks while silicon development cycles take years.
The shift toward trillion-parameter models and open-weight availability is driving a need for hardware that can handle sparse computation and rapidly changing numeric formats.

backlog.title: Thermal Co-Simulation Testing Of Co-Packaged Optics
backlog.summary:
Ensuring optical engines can operate reliably alongside high-power AI processors in multi-chip packages.
The post Thermal Co-Simulation Testing Of Co-Packaged Optics appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Co-packaged optics (CPO) are essential for scaling data center interconnects, but they introduce significant thermal management challenges in high-power AI packages.
Thermal co-simulation results demonstrate that CPO can operate reliably within a 3 kW power envelope when integrated into advanced multi-chip packages.
The design utilizes a 9-2-9 layer substrate and UCIe interfaces to support over 100 Tbps of optical bandwidth, proving that optical engines can coexist with high-performance AI silicon.

backlog.title: Beyond The Specification: What Really Determines PCIe Retimer Reach?
backlog.summary:
Multiple interacting factors span silicon design, controller intelligence, channel quality, and the transmission medium itself.
The post Beyond The Specification: What Really Determines PCIe Retimer Reach? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: PCIe retimer reach is determined by a combination of SerDes architecture, controller intelligence, and channel quality rather than just specification compliance.
While standard specifications often target 36 dB of insertion loss at Nyquist, leading retimer vendors are engineering for 40 dB or higher to provide greater deployment flexibility.
The ability to exceed standard loss budgets allows designers to accommodate more connectors, longer PCB traces, and manufacturing variations without requiring costly board redesigns.

backlog.title: AMBA C2C: Moving Forward With A Converged AMBA Foundation For C2C Connectivity
backlog.summary:
Extending chiplet connectivity across AXI and CHI with scalable protocol subsets, interoperability, and flexible transport support.
The post AMBA C2C: Moving Forward With A Converged AMBA Foundation For C2C Connectivity appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The new AMBA C2C specification aims to unify chip-to-chip connectivity by supporting both AXI and CHI protocols under a single, scalable framework.
By utilizing protocol subsetting, AMBA C2C allows implementations to scale complexity based on specific use cases, such as simple I/O attachment versus fully coherent superchips.
This converged approach addresses the need for greater reuse and interoperability across the vast installed base of AXI-based designs in the chiplet ecosystem.

backlog.title: Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind
backlog.summary: Have you ever thought about what makes you you? Science assures us it has everything to do with the three-pound organ between our ears, with its billions of neurons and trillions of delicate connections. But it’s a lot trickier to explain why we have a sense of self-awareness or to pin down precisely where that…
bullets: Technologists are exploring extreme methods for cognitive preservation, ranging from cryopreservation of brains to theoretical mind-uploading and head transplants.
While historical experiments like Robert White’s 1970s monkey head transplants provide a grim foundation, modern efforts remain mired in severe ethical, technical, and physiological hurdles.

The research into cognitive immortality serves as a speculative frontier that may yield secondary benefits in neuroscience and medical technology, even if the primary goal of consciousness transfer remains elusive.
